description: Spatial audio formats decomposed. From simple stereo through 5.1/7.1 channel surround, to object-based (Dolby Atmos), and listener-position-independent (Ambisonics, NeRF-style soundfields). The compression problem is two-fold: encode the spatial structure efficiently AND remain renderable on diverse playback systems (headphones, soundbars, full 7.1 setups).

sub_mechanisms.name: channel_based_5_1
sub_mechanisms.definition: Six discrete channels: Left, Right, Center, LFE (subwoofer), Left Surround, Right Surround. Pre-mixed for a specific 5-speaker + sub layout.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standard for movie soundtracks since the 1990s. Decoder routing is trivial: each channel goes to its named speaker. Pre-mixed means no per-listener adjustment; render exactly as authored.

sub_mechanisms.name: channel_based_7_1
sub_mechanisms.definition: Eight channels: 5.1 + Left Back + Right Back. Extends 5.1's surround imaging with additional rear channels.
sub_mechanisms.why: More precise surround imaging than 5.1. Same architecture (pre-mixed channels, fixed speaker layout) but more spatial resolution behind the listener. Common in modern movie soundtracks.

sub_mechanisms.name: dolby_atmos_objects
sub_mechanisms.definition: Object-based audio: each sound source (dialog, footsteps, ambient music) is a separate object with associated position metadata. Renderer places objects in 3D for the playback system.
sub_mechanisms.why: Mix-once, render-everywhere. The mix engineer places objects in 3D; playback (headphones, soundbar, full Atmos cinema) renders them appropriately. No pre-mixed compromise; each playback system gets a tailored render.

sub_mechanisms.name: object_metadata
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-object metadata: 3D position (x, y, z), size, gain, time-varying trajectory. Encoded as a small parameter stream.
sub_mechanisms.why: Metadata is small (~kbps) compared to audio (~hundreds of kbps). The architectural insight: encode WHERE separately from WHAT, letting playback system optimise the spatial render.

sub_mechanisms.name: bed_channels_plus_objects
sub_mechanisms.definition: Atmos and similar formats use a combination: 'bed' channels (background music, ambience) plus discrete objects (dialog, effects). The bed is channel-based; objects are object-based.
sub_mechanisms.why: Hybrid efficiency: high-channel-count background audio is cheap as bed channels; discrete sound effects benefit from object-based positioning. Combined coding handles both ends of the spectrum.

sub_mechanisms.name: ambisonics_first_order
sub_mechanisms.definition: Four channels (W, X, Y, Z) encoding a soundfield as spherical harmonics. W is omnidirectional; X, Y, Z encode directional information.
sub_mechanisms.why: Listener-position-independent: the soundfield is fully encoded. Renderer extracts the appropriate render for any output (headphones via HRTF, stereo, 5.1, 7.1, etc.). Used in 360° VR audio because the listener orientation can change.

sub_mechanisms.name: ambisonics_higher_order
sub_mechanisms.definition: Higher-order ambisonics (HOA) uses 9 channels (2nd order), 16 channels (3rd), 25 channels (4th). Each order adds finer spatial resolution.
sub_mechanisms.why: First-order ambisonics has limited spatial resolution (everything is somewhat fuzzy). Higher orders sharpen the imaging. Bit cost scales as order squared; quality gains diminish. 3rd order is common for VR; higher for research.

sub_mechanisms.name: binaural_rendering
sub_mechanisms.definition: Conversion of multi-channel or object-based audio to 2-channel headphone output, using HRTF filters to position virtual speakers in 3D.
sub_mechanisms.why: Headphones are stereo only but need to render spatial content. HRTF-based binaural rendering places virtual speakers around the listener's head, capturing inter-aural time/level differences. Quality depends heavily on HRTF accuracy.

sub_mechanisms.name: personalised_HRTF
sub_mechanisms.definition: HRTFs measured for individual listeners (via camera-based ear measurement or anthropometric models). More accurate than generic HRTFs.
sub_mechanisms.why: Generic HRTFs work but lack the precision of per-listener filters. Apple Spatial Audio uses iPhone camera measurements to approximate per-listener HRTFs; some research uses full anechoic-chamber measurements. Quality gain is substantial.

sub_mechanisms.name: lfe_low_frequency_effects
sub_mechanisms.definition: Dedicated subwoofer channel (0.1 in 5.1, 7.1, Atmos). Carries only bass content (typically below 120 Hz) but at higher peak SPL.
sub_mechanisms.why: Bass is omnidirectional (HVS can't localise low frequencies). A separate channel + dedicated woofer optimises bass reproduction without requiring full-range surround speakers. The '.1' notation reflects this special-purpose channel.

sub_mechanisms.name: atmos_height_channels
sub_mechanisms.definition: Atmos adds vertical positioning: ceiling speakers or upfiring speakers in soundbars. Objects can be positioned above the listener (rain on the roof, helicopters).
sub_mechanisms.why: Vertical localisation adds immersion. 5.1/7.1 are 2D (ear-level only); Atmos extends to 3D. The vertical positioning is what defines Atmos as 'immersive' vs 'surround' audio.

sub_mechanisms.name: codec_independent_spatial_metadata
sub_mechanisms.definition: Spatial metadata (Atmos object positions, Ambisonics matrices) is carried independently of the audio codec. The codec can be AAC, AC-3, Opus, DTS, etc.
sub_mechanisms.why: Same architecture as HDR metadata over video codecs: metadata is small and codec-agnostic. The spatial format works regardless of which underlying compression codec carries the audio. Same insight; different vertical.

derivation_rules.name: object_based_audio_renders_per_playback_system
if: audio is encoded as objects + metadata
then: each playback system gets a tailored render
derivation_rules.why: Pre-mixed channels embed a specific render (this 5.1 mix is for 5.1 systems). Object-based delays the render until playback, letting it match the actual setup. Headphones get binaural; soundbars get virtual surround; cinema gets full Atmos. Same mix, multiple renders.

derivation_rules.name: ambisonics_separates_capture_from_render
if: a soundfield is encoded as spherical harmonics
then: it can be rendered to any output regardless of original capture geometry
derivation_rules.why: Ambisonics encodes the soundfield itself, not a render of it. The renderer decodes for the specific output. Used in VR because the listener's orientation rotates the rendered soundfield in real-time — only possible with soundfield-level encoding.

derivation_rules.name: hrtf_accuracy_determines_binaural_quality
if: binaural rendering uses a generic HRTF
then: spatial imaging accuracy is limited compared to personalised HRTF
derivation_rules.why: HRTFs vary substantially between individuals (head size, ear shape, torso). Generic HRTFs are 'average' — work OK for many but mismatch many others. Personalised HRTFs are more accurate. Apple's camera-based personalisation is a deployable compromise.

derivation_rules.name: metadata_separation_enables_codec_agnostic_spatial_audio
if: spatial metadata is independent of audio compression
then: the same spatial format works across all codecs
derivation_rules.why: Decoupling metadata from compression is the standard architectural move (HDR in video, Atmos in audio). Object positions don't compress further; the audio they reference does. Independence lets each evolve separately.
